questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the major product [$P_3$] formed when n- Hexane undergoes the given series of reactions: \\ $\text{n-Hexane} \xrightarrow{\large{V_2O_5;\ 20\ atm,\ 773k}} [\text{P}_1] \xrightarrow{\large{C_2H_5Cl,\ Anhyd.AlCl_3;\ \triangle}} [\text{P}_2] \xrightarrow{\large{Conc.HNO_3 + H_2SO_4;\ 333K}} [\text{P}_3]\ \text{Major product}$
\($\mathrm{n} \text{-Hexane } \frac{\mathrm{V}_2 \mathrm{O}_5}{20 \mathrm{~atm}, 773 \mathrm{k}}\left[\mathrm{P}_{1}\right]\)
\(\left[\mathrm{P}_{1}$\right] \quad \xrightarrow[\triangle]{\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{5} $\mathrm{Cl}, \text{ Anhyd. } \mathrm{AlCl}_{3}}\left[\mathrm{P}_{2}$\right]\)
\($\left[\mathrm{P}_{2}\right] \quad \xrightarrow[333 \mathrm{~K}]{\text{ Conc. } \mathrm{HNO}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4}\left[\mathrm{P}_{3}$\right]\) Major product
questions.solution:
The first step involves the reaction of n-hexane over $V_2O_5$ at $773$ K and $20$ atm. This is an aromatization reaction where n-hexane undergoes dehydrogenation and cyclization to form benzene. Thus, $[P_1]$ is benzene (C_6H_6$).

The second step is the reaction of benzene ($[P_1]$) with ethyl chloride (C_2H_5Cl$) in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ and heat. This is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. The electrophile, ethyl cation (C_2H_5^+$), attacks the benzene ring to form ethylbenzene. Thus, $[P_2]$ is ethylbenzene (C_6H_5CH_2CH_3$).

The third step involves the reaction of ethylbenzene ($[P_2]$) with a mixture of concentrated $HNO_3$ and concentrated $H_2SO_4$ at $333$ K. This is an electrophilic aromatic nitration. The ethyl group ($-CH_2CH_3$) attached to the benzene ring is an electron-donating group due to the $+I$ effect and hyperconjugation, making it an ortho, para-directing group. Due to the steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product is formed by the attack of the nitronium ion (NO_2^+$) at the para position. Therefore, the major product $[P_3]$ is p-nitroethylbenzene.

The structure of p-nitroethylbenzene matches option (2).$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The statements given below contains assertion and reason. Choose the correct option
Assertion (A): Propene reacts with HBr in presence of organic peroxide gives 1-bromopropane.
Reason(R): The reaction occurs through carbocation intermediate
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation of A
questions.solution:
Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of an organic peroxide to give 1-bromopropane. This is known as the peroxide effect or Kharasch effect, which follows anti-Markovnikov addition. Thus, the assertion is true.

The reaction proceeds via a free radical mechanism involving a more stable secondary free radical intermediate, not a carbocation intermediate. Thus, the reason is false.

Answer: A is true but R is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product formed in the following reaction is:
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the addition of HBr to an alkene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. This proceeds via a free-radical mechanism (Kharasch effect or anti-Markovnikov addition).

First, the peroxide initiates the reaction to generate a bromine radical (Br^{\bullet}$).

The $Br^{\bullet}$ radical attacks the double bond to form the most stable carbon radical intermediate. There are two possible sites for the attack on the $HO-C_6H_4-CH=CH-CH_3$ molecule:
1. Attack at the \alpha$-carbon gives a secondary alkyl radical: $HO-C_6H_4-CH(Br)-\dot{C}H-CH_3$
2. Attack at the $\beta$-carbon gives a benzylic radical: $HO-C_6H_4-\dot{C}H-CH(Br)-CH_3$

The benzylic radical is significantly more stable due to resonance delocalization with the benzene ring (further enhanced by the electron-donating $-OH$ group). Therefore, the $Br^{\bullet}$ radical preferentially adds to the $\beta$-carbon.

The stable benzylic radical then abstracts a hydrogen atom from another HBr molecule to yield the final product:
$HO-C_6H_4-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3$

Note that the phenolic $-OH$ group does not react with HBr because the aryl $C-O$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance and is difficult to break.

Comparing this with the given options, the correct structure is represented in option (C).

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the given alkanes in increasing order of their boiling points.
(A) 2, 2-dimethylpropane
(B) 2-methylbutane
(C) $n$-pentane
(D) $n$-butane
questions.solution:
The boiling point of alkanes increases with an increase in molecular mass due to stronger van der Waals forces. Since $n$-butane (D) has four carbon atoms while the others have five, it has the lowest boiling point.

For isomeric alkanes, the boiling point decreases with an increase in branching. Branching makes the molecule more spherical, which decreases the surface area of contact and weakens the intermolecular van der Waals forces.

Among the isomers of pentane, $n$-pentane (C) is unbranched and has the highest surface area, resulting in the highest boiling point. 2-methylbutane (B) has one branch, and 2,2-dimethylpropane (A) has two branches, making it the most spherical with the lowest boiling point among the isomers.

Thus, the increasing order of boiling points is $n$-butane (D) < 2,2-dimethylpropane (A) < 2-methylbutane (B) $< n$-pentane (C).

The correct sequence is $D < A < B < C$.

Answer: $D < A < B < C$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the reagents needed to convert Benzene to 4–Bromophenylpropene in the correct sequential order.
(A). $\text{Cl}_2/\Delta$
(B). $(\text{CH}_3)_2$-CHCl /anhyd. $\text{AlCl}_3$
(C). Alc. KOH
(D). $\text{Br}_2$ / Fe
questions.solution:
The conversion of benzene to 4-bromophenylpropene involves the following sequential steps:

1. Friedel-Crafts Alkylation (Reagent B): Benzene reacts with isopropyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form isopropylbenzene (cumene).
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

2. Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (Reagent D): Isopropylbenzene undergoes bromination with $\text{Br}_2/\text{Fe}$. The isopropyl group is ortho/para-directing. Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product is 4-bromoisopropylbenzene.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Br}_2/\text{Fe} \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

3. Free Radical Halogenation (Reagent A): Treatment with $\text{Cl}_2/\Delta$ leads to substitution at the benzylic position, replacing the tertiary benzylic hydrogen with a chlorine atom to form 1-bromo-4-(2-chloropropan-2-yl)benzene.
$4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Cl}_2/\Delta \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

4. Dehydrohalogenation (Reagent C): Finally, reaction with alcoholic KOH causes E2 elimination of $\text{HCl}$, forming a double bond to yield 2-(4-bromophenyl)propene (a 4-bromophenylpropene derivative).
$4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Alc. KOH} \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$

The correct sequential order of reagents is B, D, A, C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitutions is:
questions.solution:
Reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution depends on the electron density of the benzene ring. Electron-donating groups (EDG) increase the electron density and activate the ring, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease the electron density and deactivate the ring.

Let us analyze the given compounds:
1. Compound (III) has an $-\text{OCH}_3$ group. It is a strongly activating group due to its strong $+R$ (resonance) effect, which outweighs its $-I$ effect.
2. Compound (I) has a $-\text{CH}_3$ group. It is an activating group due to its $+I$ (inductive) and $+H$ (hyperconjugation) effects. The $+R$ effect of $-\text{OCH}_3$ is stronger than the $+H$ effect of $-\text{CH}_3$, making compound (III) more reactive than compound (I).
3. Compound (II) is benzene, which has no substituents and serves as the reference.
4. Compound (IV) has a $-\text{CF}_3$ group. It is a strongly deactivating group due to its strong $-I$ effect.

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution is III > I > II > IV.

Answer: $III > I > II > IV$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound with molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$ that gives acetone on ozonolysis is:
questions.solution:
Ozonolysis of an alkene cleaves the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond to form carbonyl compounds.

Since one of the products is acetone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, the original alkene must contain a $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=$ group.

The molecular formula of the compound is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$. Subtracting the 3 carbon atoms of the acetone fragment leaves 2 carbon atoms for the other fragment, which must be an ethylidene group, $=\text{CHCH}_3$.

Combining these two fragments, the structure of the alkene is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3$, which is 2-methyl-2-butene.

The ozonolysis reaction is:
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{O}_3, \text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$

Answer: 2-methyl-2-butene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 2-butyne is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4/\text{HgSO}_4$, the product formed is:
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkyne with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\text{HgSO}_4$ is known as Kucherov's reaction, which results in the hydration of the alkyne.

For 2-butyne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3$), the addition of a water molecule across the triple bond initially forms an unstable enol intermediate.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+}, \text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$

The enol intermediate undergoes tautomerization to form the more stable keto form, which is butanone.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$

Thus, the final product is butanone.

Answer: Butanone

questions.q: The major product of acid catalysed hydration reaction of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene is:
questions.solution:
The acid-catalyzed hydration of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate. The reaction begins with the protonation of the double bond to form the more stable carbocation. Protonation of the terminal carbon of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene yields a secondary carbocation, $(CH_3)_3C-CH^{+}-CH_3$.

This secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation, $(CH_3)_2C^{+}-CH(CH_3)_2$. This rearrangement is driven by the conversion of a secondary carbocation into a more stable tertiary carbocation.

Subsequently, a water molecule acts as a nucleophile and attacks the tertiary carbocation to form the corresponding oxonium ion. Deprotonation of the oxonium ion yields the final product, 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.

Answer: 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol

questions.solution:
Reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution is determined by the electron density of the benzene ring. Substituents that increase electron density (electron-donating groups, EDG) activate the ring, while substituents that decrease electron density (electron-withdrawing groups, EWG) deactivate the ring.

Option (1): The order given is Toluene > Phenol > Benzene > p-Chlorobenzoic acid. Option (2): The order given is Toluene > Chlorobenzene > p-Nitrochlorobenzene > 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene. This is correct as the reactivity decreases with the addition of more electron-withdrawing nitro groups.

Option (3): The order given is Toluene > Benzene > Chlorobenzene > Nitrobenzene. This is correct as the methyl group activates the ring, while chlorine and the nitro group deactivate it, with the nitro group being a much stronger deactivator.

Option (4): The order given is Anisole > Toluene > Benzene > Benzotrifluoride. This is correct as the methoxy group is a strong activator (+M), the methyl group is a weak activator, and the trifluoromethyl group is a strong deactivator (-I).

Since the question asks for the incorrect order, option (1) is the correct choice.

Answer:

questions.q: An Alkene " X " on reaction with hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ gave a mixture of Ethanoic acid and Propanone. Identify " X ".
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkene with hot acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ results in oxidative cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond. The products formed depend on the substitution pattern at the double bond carbons.

Ethanoic acid is $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}$, which corresponds to a terminal $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=$ group after oxidation. Propanone is $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCH}_3$, which corresponds to a $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{C}=$ group after oxidation.

Combining these two fragments, the alkene must be $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$.

The structure $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Answer: 2- Methylbut-2-ene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkene on reductive ozonolysis gives ketones only as the product?
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of an alkene involves the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond (C=C$) to form carbonyl compounds. If the carbons involved in the double bond are substituted with two alkyl groups (i.e., tetrasubstituted or trisubstituted with alkyl groups), the products are ketones. If one or both carbons are bonded to a hydrogen atom, the products are aldehydes.

Analyzing the options:

But-2-ene (CH_3-CH=CH-CH_3$): Each carbon of the double bond is bonded to one hydrogen atom. Ozonolysis yields two molecules of acetaldehyde (CH_3CHO$), which are aldehydes.

1,2-butadiene (CH_2=C=CH-CH_3$): This is an allene. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde (HCHO$), carbon dioxide (CO_2$), and acetaldehyde (CH_3CHO$).

1,4-cyclohexadiene: The double bonds are within the ring. Ozonolysis leads to the formation of dialdehydes (specifically, succinaldehyde).

2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene ($(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$): Each carbon of the double bond is bonded to two methyl groups. Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond to produce two molecules of acetone ($(CH_3)_2C=O$), which is a ketone.

Answer: 2, 3-dimethylbut-2-ene$

questions.solution:
The reaction shown is the addition of hydrogen bromide (HBr) to propene (CH_3-CH=CH_2$).

The reaction proceeds via the electrophilic addition mechanism. In the first step, the electrophile $H^{+}$ from HBr attacks the double bond to form the more stable secondary carbocation (CH_3-CH^{+}-CH_3$).

In the second step, the nucleophile $Br^{-}$ attacks the carbocation to form 2-bromopropane (CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3$).

This follows Markovnikov's rule, which is characteristic of electrophilic addition reactions to alkenes.

Answer: Electrophilic addition$

questions.q: Identify the Alkane (molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{18}$ ) which yields only a single monochloride on Chlorination in the presence of sunlight.
questions.solution:
The formation of only a single monochloride upon chlorination implies that all hydrogen atoms in the alkane molecule are equivalent. This means the molecule must possess a high degree of symmetry such that replacing any hydrogen atom with a chlorine atom results in the same product.

Analyzing the options:

2,4-Dimethylhexane has multiple types of hydrogen atoms (primary, secondary, and tertiary), leading to multiple monochlorinated isomers.

3,4-Dimethylhexane also has multiple types of hydrogen atoms, leading to multiple monochlorinated isomers.

2,2,3,3-Tetramethylbutane has a structure where all 18 hydrogen atoms are equivalent. Specifically, it consists of two tert-butyl groups connected by a central C-C bond. Each of the four methyl groups attached to the quaternary carbons is equivalent, and there are no other types of hydrogens. Thus, chlorination yields only one monochloride, 1-chloro-2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane.

2,2,4-Trimethylpentane (isooctane) has several distinct types of hydrogen atoms (primary, secondary, and tertiary), leading to multiple monochlorinated products.

Therefore, 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane is the correct alkane.

Answer: 2, 2, 3, 3-Tetramethylbutane

questions.q:
Identify the final product $[\mathrm{Y}]$ in the following reaction.
$[\mathrm{X}]+\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow[293 \mathrm{ K}]{\mathrm{OH}^{-}}[\mathrm{Y}]$
questions.solution:
The reaction of $p$-nitrotoluene with $CrO_2Cl_2$ in $CS_2$ followed by hydrolysis is the Etard reaction, which oxidizes the methyl group to an aldehyde. Thus, $[X]$ is $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde (O_2N-C_6H_4-CHO$).

The subsequent reaction is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation between $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde and acetophenone (C_6H_5COCH_3$) in the presence of a base (OH^-$).

The base abstracts an \alpha$-hydrogen from acetophenone to form an enolate ion, which then performs a nucleophilic attack on the carbonyl carbon of $p$-nitrobenzaldehyde. This is followed by dehydration to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone.

The product $[Y]$ is $p$-nitrobenzalacetophenone, which has the structure $O_2N-C_6H_4-CH=CH-CO-C_6H_5$.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of reactivity of halogens with alkanes is:
questions.solution:
The reactivity of halogens towards alkanes is determined by the bond dissociation energy of the halogen molecule and the enthalpy of the reaction. The reaction of an alkane with a halogen is represented as $R-H + X_2 \rightarrow R-X + H-X$.

The reactivity order is governed by the strength of the $H-X$ bond formed and the ease of breaking the $X-X$ bond. Fluorine is the most reactive due to its high electronegativity and the high bond energy of the $H-F$ bond formed, which makes the reaction highly exothermic. Iodine is the least reactive because the reaction is endothermic and the $H-I$ bond is relatively weak.

The experimental order of reactivity for halogens with alkanes is $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$.

Answer: $F_2 > C l_2 > B r_2 > I_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of grams of bromine that will completely react with 5 g of pentene is:
[Atomic mass of $\mathrm{Br}=80 \mathrm{u}$ ]
questions.solution:
The chemical formula for pentene is $C_{5}H_{10}$. The reaction of pentene with bromine is an addition reaction:

$C_{5}H_{10} + Br_{2} \rightarrow C_{5}H_{10}Br_{2}$

The molar mass of pentene (C_{5}H_{10}$) is 5 \times 12 + 10 \times 1 = 70$ g/mol.

The molar mass of bromine (Br_{2}$) is 2 \times 80 = 160$ g/mol.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, 1 mole of pentene reacts with 1 mole of bromine. Therefore, 70 g of pentene reacts with 160 g of bromine.

For 5 g of pentene, the mass of bromine required is:

Mass of $Br_{2} = \dfrac{160}{70} \times 5 = \dfrac{800}{70} = \dfrac{80}{7} \approx 11.428$ g.

Rounding to the nearest provided option, the value is 11.4 g.

Answer: 11.4 g

questions.q: An unsaturated hydrocarbon $[\mathrm{A}]$ undergoes the following series of reactions. Identify $[\mathrm{A}]$.
questions.solution:
The hydrocarbon [A] reacts with ammoniacal $AgNO_3$ to give no reaction, which indicates that it is not a terminal alkyne. This eliminates but-1-yne and propyne.

The reaction of [A] with $Na/liquid NH_3$ gives a trans product, which is a characteristic reaction of internal alkynes to form trans-alkenes. This suggests [A] is an internal alkyne.

The reaction of [A] with alkaline $KMnO_4$ at 383 K yields 2 moles of a carboxylic acid with formula $C_2H_4O_2$, which is acetic acid (CH_3COOH$). This implies that the oxidative cleavage of the triple bond in [A] produces two molecules of acetic acid. For an internal alkyne $R-C \equiv C-R$ to yield two molecules of $CH_3COOH$, the structure must be $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$, which is but-2-yne.

Ozonolysis of but-2-yne (CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$) followed by $Zn/H_2O$ yields a diketone, specifically butane-2,3-dione (CH_3COCOCH_3$), which matches the description of [B].

Therefore, [A] is but-2-yne.

Answer: But-2-yne$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The Electrophilic addition to an unsymmetrical alkene always occurs through the formation of a more stable Carbanion intermediate.

Between the two alkenes - (i) $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2-\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ and (ii). $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$, compound (i) will show geometrical isomerism
Greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the double bonded Carbon atoms, the less stable is the alkene.
The major product formed when 2-Methylpropene reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is tert. butyl alcohol.
questions.solution:
Electrophilic addition to an unsymmetrical alkene proceeds via the formation of a more stable carbocation intermediate, not a carbanion. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

For geometrical isomerism, each carbon atom of the double bond must be attached to two different groups. In compound (i), $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$, the carbon atom on the left is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism. Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

According to the stability of alkenes, the stability increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the double-bonded carbon atoms due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects. Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

When 2-methylpropene, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2$, reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$, the reaction follows Markovnikov's rule. The proton adds to the terminal carbon to form the more stable tert-butyl carbocation, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrmC^{+}$, which then reacts with water to form tert-butyl alcohol, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{COH}$. Thus, the fourth statement is correct.

Answer: The major product formed when 2-Methylpropene reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is tert. butyl alcohol.

questions.q:
Convert Benzene → 3-Bromophenol by choosing appropriate reagents $[(i)$ to (v)] in the correct sequence.
$(i)\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}\left(0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\right) \quad (ii) Conc. \mathrm{HNO}_3 / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \quad (iii) \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} / 283 \mathrm{ K} \quad (iv) \mathrm{Fe} / \mathrm{HCl} \quad (v) \mathrm{Br} 2 / \mathrm{Fe}$
questions.solution:
The conversion of benzene to 3-bromophenol requires the introduction of a meta-directing group followed by bromination, or the use of a group that directs meta and can be converted to a hydroxyl group. Since the hydroxyl group is ortho/para-directing, it must be introduced after the bromine atom is placed in the meta position.

Nitration of benzene using $Conc. HNO_3 / H_2SO_4$ (reagent ii) gives nitrobenzene.

Bromination of nitrobenzene using $Br_2 / Fe$ (reagent v) gives 1-bromo-3-nitrobenzene because the nitro group is meta-directing.

Reduction of the nitro group using $Fe / HCl$ (reagent iv) gives 3-bromoaniline.

Diazotization of 3-bromoaniline using $NaNO_2 / HCl$ at $0^{{}^{\circ}}C$ (reagent i) gives 3-bromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Hydrolysis of the diazonium salt using $H_2O / 283 K$ (reagent iii) gives 3-bromophenol.

The correct sequence is ii, v, iv, i, iii.

Answer: ii, v, iv, i, iii

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their reactivity when each of them is reacted with chloroethane / anhydrous AlC$l_3$.
questions.solution:
The reaction of chloroethane with anhydrous $AlCl_{3}$ is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. This reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the benzene ring acts as a nucleophile. The reactivity of the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution depends on the electron density of the ring. Electron-donating groups increase the electron density and thus increase the reactivity, while electron-withdrawing groups decrease the electron density and decrease the reactivity.

Let us analyze the substituents on the benzene rings:
Compound [A] is benzene, which has no substituents.
Compound [B] is bromobenzene. The $-Br$ group is deactivating due to its strong inductive effect ($-I$) which outweighs its resonance effect ($+M$) in terms of overall reactivity towards electrophilic substitution.
Compound [C] is p-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene). The two $-CH_{3}$ groups are electron-donating via inductive effect ($+I$) and hyperconjugation, significantly increasing the electron density of the ring.
Compound [D] is nitrobenzene. The $-NO_{2}$ group is a very strong electron-withdrawing group due to both $-I$ and $-M$ effects, making the ring highly deactivated.

Comparing the reactivity:
Nitrobenzene [D] is the least reactive due to the strong deactivating $-NO_{2}$ group.
Bromobenzene [B] is less reactive than benzene [A] because $-Br$ is deactivating.
Benzene [A] is less reactive than p-xylene [C] because p-xylene has two activating methyl groups.

Therefore, the increasing order of reactivity is D < B < A < C.

Answer: D < B < A < C

Compound [A] reacts with cold, dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ to form 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol. This reaction is a syn-hydroxylation of an alkene. The structure of 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol is $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(OH)(CH}_{3})-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_{3}$. The corresponding alkene [A] is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which has the structure $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(CH}_{3})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_{3}$.

Reaction of 2-methylbut-2-ene with hot $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ (oxidative cleavage) breaks the double bond: $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(CH}_{3})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_{3} \xrightarrow{\text{hot KMnO}_{4}} \text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_{3} + \text{CH}_{3}-\text{COOH}$. Here, $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{COOH}$ is acetic acid and [D] is propanone ($\text{CH}_{3}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_{3}$).

Reaction of 2-methylbut-2-ene with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov addition. The radical mechanism leads to the formation of 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, as the bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon of the double bond to form the more stable secondary radical intermediate.

Answer: [A] 2-Methylbut-2-ene [B] 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane [D] Propanone

Ethyl cyclohexane has the molecular formula $C_8H_{16}$. The structure consists of a cyclohexane ring with an ethyl group attached at one position.

Counting the distinct positions for chlorine substitution:
1. Alpha-carbon of ethyl group: 1 isomer.

4. Ortho position on ring: 1 isomer.
5. Meta position on ring: 1 isomer.
6. Para position on ring: 1 isomer.

Total number of mono-chloro derivatives = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.

Answer: 6

questions.q:
From among the following, identify the compound which forms two moles of a ketone on ozonolysis.
[A] 2,3-Dimethylbutane.
[B] 3-Methyl-1-pentene.
[C] 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene.
[D] 2-Methyl-2-pentane.
questions.solution:
Ozonolysis of an alkene involves the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond to form carbonyl compounds. The general reaction is $R_1R_2C=CR_3R_4 \xrightarrow{O_3, Zn/H_2O} R_1R_2C=O + R_3R_4C=O$.

For the product to be two moles of a ketone, the alkene must be symmetric and substituted such that each carbon of the double bond is attached to two alkyl groups.

Analyzing the options:
[A] 2,3-Dimethylbutane is an alkane and does not undergo ozonolysis.
[B] 3-Methyl-1-pentene is $CH_2=CH-CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde ($HCHO$) and 2-methylbutanal.
[C] 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene is $(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$. Ozonolysis yields two moles of acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$), which is a ketone.
[D] 2-Methyl-2-pentene (assuming the intended structure) is $(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_2CH_3$. Ozonolysis yields acetone and propanal.

Answer: [C]

Partial hydrogenation of propyne to propene using $H_2 / Pd$ (Lindlar catalyst or poisoned Pd).

Aromatization of n-hexane to benzene using $Cr_2O_3$ at high temperature and pressure.
$CH_3(CH_2)_4CH_3 \xrightarrow{Cr_2O_3, \Delta, P} C_6H_6 + 4H_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following will show geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Geometrical isomerism is exhibited by alkenes if both carbon atoms of the double bond are attached to two different groups.

For 2-methylbut-2-ene, the structure is $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$. One carbon of the double bond is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

For 1,2-dibromopropene, the structure is $CH_3-C(Br)=CH-Br$. The first carbon is attached to a methyl group and a bromine atom, while the second carbon is attached to a hydrogen atom and a bromine atom. Since both carbons have two different groups attached, it exhibits geometrical isomerism.

For cyclohexene, the ring strain prevents the formation of a trans-isomer in a six-membered ring, and it exists only in the cis-form.

For 2-methylpropene, the structure is $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$. The first carbon is attached to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 1,2-dibromopropene

questions.q: Total number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds in ethene molecule is
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of ethene is $C_{2}H_{4}$. The structural formula is $CH_{2}=CH_{2}$.

In the molecule, there are four $C-H$ single bonds and one $C=C$ double bond.

Each single bond consists of one $\sigma$ bond. Thus, there are four $\sigma$ bonds from the $C-H$ bonds.

The $C=C$ double bond consists of one $\sigma$ bond and one $\pi$ bond.

Total $\sigma$ bonds = $4$ (from $C-H$) + $1$ (from $C=C$) = $5\sigma$ bonds.

Total $\pi$ bonds = $1$ (from $C=C$) = $1\pi$ bond.

Answer: $5 \sigma$ and $1 \pi$ bonds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Coupling reaction is an example of
questions.solution:
Coupling reactions, such as the formation of azo dyes from diazonium salts and aromatic compounds (like phenols or amines), involve the attack of a diazonium cation on an electron-rich aromatic ring.

The diazonium cation, $Ar-N_{2}^{+}$, acts as a weak electrophile. It attacks the electron-rich aromatic ring, which acts as a nucleophile.

This process results in the replacement of a hydrogen atom on the aromatic ring by the diazonium group, which is a characteristic feature of electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Therefore, the coupling reaction is classified as an electrophilic substitution reaction.

Answer: electrophilic substitution reaction.

questions.solution:
The Wurtz reaction $2R$-$X + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R$-$R + 2NaX$ is effective only for symmetrical alkanes (even carbon count). Using two different alkyl halides gives a mixture of three products (R-R, R-R', R'-R'), making it ineffective for unsymmetrical alkanes.

(1) 2,7-dimethyloctane: Symmetrical — can be split into two identical isopentyl fragments. Can be prepared effectively.

(3) 1,4-dicyclohexylbutane: Symmetrical around the center. Can be prepared effectively.

(4): Symmetrical structure with two identical cyclopentyl-cyclohexyl fragments. Can be prepared effectively.

(2) 2,5-dimethylheptane: Unsymmetrical with 9 carbons (odd number). Cannot be split into two identical alkyl fragments, so it requires two different alkyl halides, yielding a mixture of products.

The hydrocarbon that cannot be prepared effectively by Wurtz reaction is option (2).
